script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Workplace
Theme: small-town life

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. JOHNSON & SONS WAREHOUSE - DAY

JIM (30s, wearing a red flannel shirt, jeans, and boots) stands in the center of the spacious, dimly lit room. He's surrounded by stacks of boxes filled with various household goods. A faint hum of machinery can be heard in the background.

JIM
(whispering to himself)
I can't believe I'm here...

Footsteps echo through the warehouse. JIM turns to face the entrance. A middle-aged woman named MARY (wearing a blue apron) approaches, pushing a cart full of boxes.

MARY
(smiling)
Hi, Jim. Welcome to Johnson & Sons. You must be our new packer.

JIM
(nervously)
Hi, Mary. Yes, that's right. I got the job.

MARY
(encouragingly)
Don't worry, it won't be as intimidating as it looks. Just follow the instructions in the manual and ask for help when you need it.

JIM
(gratefully)
Thanks, Mary. I appreciate your support.

They share a brief moment of understanding.

INT. JOHNSON & SONS OFFICE - LATER

Jim sits at a small desk in the cramped office, surrounded by employees sorting paperwork. He stares at the instruction manual, trying to familiarize himself with the processes.

JIM
(mumbling to himself)
Box this, label that...

Suddenly, the door bursts open, and RALPH (40s, a portly man with a mustache) enters, panting.

RALPH
(angrily)
What's the holdup, new guy? I need those boxes sorted and packed as soon as possible!

JIM
(nervously)
I'll do my best, Ralph. I'm still learning the ropes.

RALPH
(disbelieving)
Learning the ropes? At your age? Get moving, Jim! We've got deadlines to meet!

JIM
(defensively)
I'll work as fast as I can, but I won't compromise the quality of the work.

RALPH
(sighs, then calmly)
Fine, but don't let me down. I'll be checking on you.

Ralph exits, leaving Jim feeling both challenged and determined.

INT. JOHNSON & SONS CANTEEN - LUNCH

Jim sits at a table, eating a lunch brought from home. Mary approaches, joining him.

MARY
(smiling)
Hey there, how's your first day going?

JIM
(sighs)
It's been a challenge. I'm trying to get the hang of things. But there's a lot to learn, and everyone seems in a hurry.

MARY
(sympathetically)
It can be overwhelming at first. But remember, Rome wasn't built in a day. And this town moves at its own pace. You'll get the hang of it.

JIM
(smiling)
Thanks, Mary. Your words mean a lot to me.

INT. JOHNSON & SONS WAREHOUSE - AFTERNOON

Jim works diligently, packing boxes efficiently. He glances over at Mary, who's sorting paperwork nearby. She catches his eye and gives him a reassuring smile.

Suddenly, the lights flicker and go out. The room is plunged into darkness. Jim curses under his breath, but Mary remains calm.

MARY
(serene)
Don't worry, Jim. It's probably just a power outage. We'll just have to finish the day the old-fashioned way.

Jim looks at her, surprised but willing to give it a try. They continue working by the dim light of their cellphones until the power is restored.

EXT. SMALL-TOWN STREET - NIGHT

The sun sets over the small town. Jim walks home, weary but satisfied with his day's work. He passes by familiar faces, greeting them with a friendly nod or wave.

Jim realizes that, despite the challenges, he's starting to feel at home in this small town. He's becoming a part of something bigger than himself.

FADE OUT.

THE END
